title: Aft Engine Mount Shear Tie — Installation

issue.reason: Original issue of the aft engine mount shear tie installation task.

abstract: Installation of the one-piece aft engine mount shear tie on the pylon rib, with the single torque sequence, the clearance checks and the load path verification that closes the task.

sections.purpose: This task gives the installation of the aft engine mount shear tie on the pylon and the load path check that must be done before the engine load is returned to the mount.
sections.job_setup_note: The pylon rib land must have been inspected and accepted by the removal task. Fasteners are single use and must come from the kit or from bonded stores; recovered fasteners must not be re-used. The joint is torqued as one pattern from the centre outward and the sequence is on the joint diagram.
sections.procedure: 1. WARNING: KEEP THE ENGINE LOAD ON THE TROLLEY UNTIL THE LOAD PATH CHECK HAS PASSED. 2. Clean the pylon rib land and apply the anti-seize compound to the faying surfaces. 3. Offer the shear tie D5450123089978 inboard past the pylon rib and align it on the two locating pins. 4. Position the forward cleat CID666183-16 and align it with the drilled pattern. 5. Install the washers AES161398-12 under each nut on the outboard face. 6. CAUTION: DO NOT RE-USE A RECOVERED FASTENER. EVERY FASTENER IN THIS JOINT IS SINGLE USE. 7. Torque the joint from the centre outward in three passes to the final value given on the joint diagram. 8. Check the clearance from the joint to the mount microswitch 152PP and to the position actuator 498PP5 and confirm both are inside the limits. 9. Reconnect the harness support. 10. Do the engine mount load path check with the trolley load released in stages. 11. Install the pylon fairing panels, the closing rib and the pylon lower access panel. 12. Close the fan cowl doors.
sections.close_out: Return the engine load to the mount only after the load path check has passed. Make sure that the fan cowl doors latch correctly and that no tool is left in the pylon. Record the installed standard, the torque values and the clearance measurements in the aircraft technical record.

safety_precautions: Keep the engine load on the trolley until the load path check has passed.
Put the fan cowl doors on their stays.
Use eye protection when the anti-seize compound is applied.

tooling.description: Drill jig, two-piece shear tie pattern

title: Aft Engine Mount Shear Tie — Installation

issue.reason: Installation re-written for the two-piece standard with the splice joint torqued before the rib joint and a re-check of the splice torque after the mount is loaded.

abstract: Installation of the aft engine mount shear tie in either standard, with the splice joint of the two-piece assembly torqued before the rib joint and re-checked once the mount carries load again.

sections.purpose: This task gives the installation of the aft engine mount shear tie on the pylon and the load path check that must be done before the engine load is returned to the mount.
sections.job_setup_note: The pylon rib land must have been inspected and accepted by the removal task. Fasteners are single use and must come from the kit or from bonded stores; recovered fasteners must not be re-used. The two-piece standard has two joints, not one, and their order is not a matter of preference: the splice joint between the halves is torqued while the assembly is still unloaded, and only then is the assembly torqued to the rib. Torquing the rib joint first locks the halves in the position they happen to be in and leaves the splice carrying a built-in offset that shows up as a fretting finding two checks later.
sections.procedure: 1. WARNING: KEEP THE ENGINE LOAD ON THE TROLLEY UNTIL THE LOAD PATH CHECK HAS PASSED. 2. Clean the pylon rib land and apply the anti-seize compound to the faying surfaces. 3. On the two-piece standard, position each half of the shear tie loosely on the rib, fit the splice plate D5450121271272 across them and torque the splice joint first, in two passes, with the halves free to settle. 4. On the one-piece standard, offer the shear tie D5450123089978 inboard past the pylon rib and align it on the two locating pins. 5. Position the forward cleat CID666183-16 and align it with the drilled pattern. 6. Install the washers AES161398-12 under each nut on the outboard face. 7. CAUTION: DO NOT RE-USE A RECOVERED FASTENER. EVERY FASTENER IN THIS JOINT IS SINGLE USE. 8. Torque the rib joint in the sequence given for the fitted standard, in three passes to the final value. 9. Check the clearance from the joint to the mount microswitch 152PP and to the position actuator 498PP5 and confirm both are inside the limits. 10. Reconnect the harness support in the position given for the fitted standard. 11. Do the engine mount load path check with the trolley load released in stages. 12. On the two-piece standard, re-check the splice joint torque with the mount load returned and record both readings; a reading below the check value means the halves settled under load and the joint is taken apart and re-built. 13. Install the pylon lower access panel and close the fan cowl doors.
sections.close_out: Return the engine load to the mount only after the load path check has passed. Make sure that the fan cowl doors latch correctly and that no tool is left in the pylon. Record the installed standard, the torque values and the clearance measurements in the aircraft technical record.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The two-piece standard has a splice joint that is torqued before the rib joint and re-checked after the mount is loaded; the one-piece standard has one joint and no re-check.

safety_precautions: Keep the engine load on the trolley until the load path check has passed.
Put the fan cowl doors on their stays.
Use eye protection when the anti-seize compound is applied.

tooling.description: Drill jig, two-piece shear tie pattern
